_note: Hand-written market take, refreshed twice a day (~8am and ~8pm UTC) by a separate scheduled research pass. Not touched by scripts/sync.py's automatic hourly sync. This is the site's hero paragraph (first thing under the H1 title). Not financial advice.
text: Bitcoin has clawed back to about $86,000, up sharply from June's $58,000 low, and the bounce looks driven by something more durable than a short squeeze. The Federal Reserve actually raised rates a quarter point on September 16, pushing the benchmark to 4%, yet crypto shrugged it off and kept climbing, a sign the market had already priced in tighter policy and is now looking past it. Treasury's shift toward buying more long-dated bonds has revived the old flight-to-hard-assets trade, pulling money into Bitcoin as a hedge against inflation and government debt worries. Institutional demand backs that up: spot Bitcoin ETFs pulled in nearly $1.6 billion over the past week, including a single-day haul of about $1 billion on Friday, and Strategy just resumed buying after a three-week pause, pushing its stash toward 846,000 coins. Analysts note big institutions are still underweight crypto, which suggests this wave of buying may have room to keep going rather than being played out. A new SEC pilot opening today lets institutions trade tokenized versions of real stocks on-chain, a small but real step toward crypto infrastructure becoming part of normal finance. Taken together the setup leans bullish into month-end, but moves this size mean a rough couple of days on weak jobs or housing data this week wouldn't be shocking, and this is a read on the situation, not financial advice.
